newsitem.title: USA: Russia signs 1997 deal with IMF - Russian source.
newsitem.headline: Russia signs 1997 deal with IMF - Russian source.

text.p: Russia and the International Monetary Fund have completed work on their 1997 policy statement and Central Bank head Sergei Dubinin signed the deal on Tuesday, an official with Russia's IMF delegation said.

The source, who asked not to be identified, said the 1997 statement set a series of targets for economic performance. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was expected to sign the document soon on behalf of the government.
"It sets fiscal targets for revenues and the deficit on a quarterly basis," he said.

The IMF delayed paying several tranches of its loan to Russia at the start of this year because it was worried about low tax revenues. Officials have said they expect to disburse the first of a new series of quarterly tranches next months.
The Russian source said the new programme aimed at annual inflation of 12 percent this year. Consumer prices rose almost 22 percent in 1996, down from 131 percent in 1995.
International Monetary Fund deputy managing director Stanley Fischer said reforms by Russia's new economic team could begin to pay off in three to six months.

"The new russian team is really a remarkably good one and they have made a very determined start on dealing with these problems, particularly the revenue problem," Fischer told Reuters Financial Television.
"We are confident that the measures they have taken so far will begin to pay off, possible in three to six months," he said.
Deputy Finance Minister Oleg Vyugin said Russia still hopes to finalise the reconciliation of its debts to the London Club of commercial bank creditors by August.
"We have said that it should all be cleared by August and we are still aiming at that," he told Reuters.
Reconciliation of the debts is essential to complete the rescheduling of Russia's London Club debts. It clarifies how much Russia owes to each individual bank creditor.
